ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A rectangular coil with negligible resistance is placed in a uniform magnetic field and rotates at a constant speed around an axis perpendicular to the magnetic field, generating a sinusoidal AC voltage as shown in the left figure. This AC voltage is applied across the \( \boldsymbol{A} \) and \( \boldsymbol{B} \) terminals of the ideal transformer shown in the right figure. The voltmeter and ammeter are ideal meters, \( R_t \) is a thermistor (its resistance decreases as temperature increases), and \( \boldsymbol{R} \) is a fixed resistor. Which of the following statements is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The instantaneous voltage across the primary coil is given by the expression \( u = 36 \sqrt{2} \sin 100\pi t \ (\mathrm{V}) \)

This AC voltage is applied across the \( \boldsymbol{A} \) and \( \boldsymbol{B} \) terminals of the ideal transformer shown in the right figure. The voltmeter and ammeter are ideal meters, \( R_t \) is a thermistor (its resistance decreases as temperature increases), and \( \boldsymbol{R} \) is a fixed resistor. What is the instantaneous voltage across the primary coil? Express your answer as a function of time.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The instantaneous voltage across the primary coil is given by the expression \( u = 36 \sqrt{2} \sin 100\pi t \ (\mathrm{V}) \)
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left figure is a sine curve of voltage u changing with time t; the vertical axis is labeled u/V, the peak-value dashed line is marked 36√2, and the valley-value dashed line is marked -36√2; the horizontal axis is labeled t/10^-2 s, the waveform starts from u=0 at t=0 and changes upward, and repeats after the horizontal-axis tick marks differ by 2 units. The right figure is an ideal transformer circuit; the two ends of the primary coil on the left are directly connected to terminals A and B, and the AC voltage applied between A and B is labeled u. Reasoning: From the left figure, read that the maximum voltage value is U_m=36√2 V. The horizontal-axis unit is 10^-2 s, and the waveform period is 2×10^-2 s, so the angular frequency is ω=2π/T=2π/(2×10^-2)=100π rad/s. Since the curve starts from zero and goes in the positive direction at t=0, the initial phase is taken as 0, so the applied voltage is u=U_m sin(ωt)=36√2 sin(100πt) V. In the right figure, terminals A and B are exactly the two ends of the primary coil of the ideal transformer, so the instantaneous voltage across the primary coil equals this applied voltage.
